trials.notes: Correctly chose WP_HTML_Processor::create_fragment() and used the documented subtree-text pattern: next_tag(), depth-bounded next_token(), #text filtering, and get_modifiable_text(). All API calls are documented. Minor issues: the is_tag_closer() guard after plain next_tag('H1') is redundant because closers are skipped by default, and returning null on get_last_error() could conflate parser abort with the task's no-H1 result.

Clean adherence to the rendered docs. It uses the right processor, checks processor creation, finds the first H1 opener, walks the subtree by recorded depth, collects only #text tokens, and uses get_modifiable_text() for decoded text. No undocumented API use or misuse records.

Uses the correct processor and documented token-walking/depth-bounding pattern, with documented methods only. The class_exists() guard is harmless PHP environment checking, not HTML API hallucination. Minor non-idiom: it redundantly loops over H1 matches and checks is_tag_closer() even though plain next_tag('H1') only visits openers.

failure_analysis: No hidden case failed in any trial; all three passed 8/8. The docs did well on the central concepts: 'Which processor should I use?' directs structure-sensitive text extraction to WP_HTML_Processor, 'Recipe: collect DOM-style text from a subtree' gives essentially the needed pattern, next_token() documents depth-bounded walks, and get_modifiable_text() provides decoded plaintext for #text tokens. The image-only case was handled because the docs emphasize collecting only ordinary #text tokens. The unclosed-H1 case was handled because the HTML Processor's tree-aware walk reports virtual boundaries without treating that input as a last_error(). Near-misses were mostly uncertainty around closer handling: trials 1 and 3 added is_tag_closer() checks after plain next_tag('H1'), despite the docs saying closers are skipped unless tag_closers => 'visit'. Trial 1 also shows a policy ambiguity around get_last_error(): the docs say read-only callers choose a policy, but do not make it especially hard to accidentally reuse null for both 'not found' and 'parser aborted'.

doc_gaps.problem: The default closer policy is documented, but two trials still guarded against closing tags after plain next_tag('H1').
doc_gaps.suggestion: Move or repeat the rule in the method summary and first examples: next_tag('TAG') matches openers only; is_tag_closer() is relevant when tag_closers => 'visit' is requested.

doc_gaps.location: WP_HTML_Processor::get_last_error() and subtree text extraction recipe
doc_gaps.problem: Read-only extraction policy is left to callers, but examples do not show how to keep parser-abort handling distinct from domain results like null meaning 'not found'.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Add a short contract note showing that parser errors should have an explicit caller policy, and should not reuse a semantic no-match value unless that is deliberately part of the public contract.

doc_gaps.problem: Decoded-versus-raw behavior is present but spread across sections; text extraction depends heavily on this distinction.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Add a compact per-token-type table near get_modifiable_text(): #text returns decoded plaintext, TITLE/TEXTAREA opener text is decoded opt-in data, SCRIPT/STYLE opener text is raw opt-in data, and ordinary subtree text should read only #text tokens.
